correctness.rationale: Every proper nontrivial subgroup of H=C_(p^2)xC_p has order p or p^2. The unique E=H[p], p order-p^2 cyclic subgroups with common P, and p other order-p lines yield a K_(p+2) clique plus p pendant vertices at E. A zero-forcing initial blue set must omit at most one leaf and one noncentral clique vertex; this is also sufficient since p>=2 supplies a blue leaf to force the center if needed. White complement generating polynomial (1+pt)(1+(p+1)t)(1+t) reverses to u^(2p-1)(u+p)(u+p+1)(u+1). Independent full subset enumeration for primes 2,3,5,7 verifies classification and coefficients, with arbitrary-prime algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: Boyer, Brimkov, English et al, The zero forcing polynomial of a graph (2018 preprint, published 2019), primary FULL text Section 4.2 Theorem 10 classifies zero forcing sets of EVERY threshold graph and Theorem 12 derives every zero forcing polynomial. A (p+2,p) pineapple is the threshold graph of 1^(p+1) 0^p 1. Applying their Theorem 10 forces at most one omitted vertex from each of the three blocks and its second condition is automatic for p>=2, giving exactly the submitted white-set classification and polynomial. This is decisive mathematically stronger prior coverage even without the word pineapple in title or formula.
